# Backend: Python data (polars or NumPy, marimo, Plotly)

`backend/pipeline/`: loading (`sources.py`), transformations (`transforms.py`), figures
(`figures.py`); `backend/notebooks/`: marimo notebooks; `backend/data/`: data (`sample/` is
committed). Explore: `kiln dev` (or `uv run marimo edit notebooks`); check: `kiln check`.

## Data chain

- **[PIPELINE]** All data follows one chain, one module per stage: `pipeline/sources.py` loads
  and validates, `pipeline/transforms.py` transforms, `pipeline/figures.py` draws. A stage never
  calls the previous one: it receives its input as a parameter.
- **[PURE-FUNCTIONS]** A transformation receives its data (`DataFrame`, NumPy array, image) and
  returns new data: no file read, no write, no global state. So it is tested without a disk.
- **[POLARS]** Tabular data: polars by default, in expressions (`pl.col(...)`) and lazy
  (`scan_*`, `.lazy()`) once the volume calls for it. Numeric arrays (images, signals, matrices,
  model weights): NumPy, vectorised, no Python loop over elements. pandas only when a library
  demands it, converted at the edge (`to_pandas()` at the last moment).
- **[DATA-SCHEMA]** Each dataset loaded is validated at the edge ([VALIDATE-AT-BOUNDARIES]):
  columns and types declared in a `pl.Schema` for a tabular set; shape, type and bounds checked
  for an array or a binary file. An explicit failure through a dedicated exception
  (`DatasetSchemaError`) when the file changes shape: loading fails, not the figure.

## Data

- **[DATA-SOURCES]** Each dataset has its source (link, retrieval date, licence) written in
  `data/README.md`.
- **[LARGE-DATA]** `data/raw/` and `data/interim/` stay out of the repository; only what is small
  and reproducible is committed: `data/sample/`, and `data/models/` for a trained model (1 MB at
  most per file, with its training command in `data/README.md`). A raw dataset is fetched by a
  function of `pipeline/sources.py`, never by an undescribed manual download.
- **[REPRODUCIBLE]** A figure is regenerated by a command from the source data; never a manual
  touch-up of a generated file. Every random draw takes a fixed seed.
- **[MODEL-TRACED]** A committed model comes with its manifest, written by the training command
  (`pipeline.models.write_manifest`: hash of the training code, seed, dataset version, metrics).
  `tests/test_models.py` fails when that code changed since (retrain, or rewrite the manifest and
  say why in the commit) and, once its evaluator is in `pipeline.models.EVALUATORS`, when the
  model scores below its recorded metrics.

## Notebooks and figures

- **[NOTEBOOKS]** Notebooks are marimo files (`notebooks/*.py`), readable in a diff. A notebook
  explores; the code that produces a delivered figure lives in `pipeline/`, which the notebook
  imports. No function longer than [FUNCTION-SIZE] in a cell.
- **[FIGURES]** One function per figure in `pipeline/figures.py`, which receives already
  transformed data and returns a Plotly `go.Figure`: a title, axes titled with their unit.
- **[ACCESSIBLE-FIGURES]** A colour-blind-safe palette (`COLORBLIND_PALETTE`), never information
  carried by colour alone, alternative text for every published figure.

## Code and tests

- **[LOGGING]** No `print()` in `pipeline/`: the result of a stage is its return value; a log,
  when one is needed, goes through `structlog` (checked).
- **[TESTS]** Every function of `pipeline/` has its tests, on small datasets written in the test
  (`DataFrame`, array), edge cases included (empty, missing value, unexpected type).
- **[REGRESSION-TEST]** Every bug fix comes with the test that would have caught it.
- **[NO-NETWORK]** No test downloads data.
- **[PROPERTY-TESTS]** Computations with invariants (aggregations, period bounds, totals,
  percentages) also have property-based tests (`hypothesis`).
